prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objective “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your case (single tooth vs full-arch), who does the surgical placement (periodontist or oral surgeon) and who restores the crown (general dentist or prosthodontist), your medical history, budget, and location. I can help you find top options in Phoenix if you want, but first here’s how to pick the best clinician for you and what to ask at a consult.

What to look for
- Specialty and training: oral & maxillofacial surgeons, periodontists, and prosthodontists have additional training in implants and complex restorations. Many general dentists place implants too — check their training and experience.  
- Experience: number of implants placed per year and experience with cases like yours (single tooth, immediate placement, full-arch, bone grafting, sinus lifts).  
- Technology: cone beam CT (CBCT) for 3D imaging, guided implant surgery, digital impressions — these improve planning and outcomes.  
- Case examples & references: before/after photos, and willingness to share patient references or reviews.  
- Team coordination: who will place the implant and who will make the final crown? Good communication between surgeon and restorative dentist is important.  
- Implant systems: reputable implant brands (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer/BioHorizons, etc.) have long-term data.  
- Comfort and sedation options: IV or oral sedation if you’re anxious or need longer procedures.  
- Follow-up care & warranty: ask about post-op follow-up, management of complications, and any restoration/implant warranties.  
- Reviews and reputation: check Google, Healthgrades, Yelp, and professional referrals.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants have you placed and how many similar cases have you done?  
- Will you take a CBCT and show me the treatment plan?  
- Who will restore the crown — you or a prosthodontist?  
- What brand/type of implant do you use and why?  
- What are all expected costs (surgery, implant, abutment, crown, grafting, imaging)?  
- What are the risks and typical complications, and how are they handled?  
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?

Typical price range (approximate)
- Single implant, abutment and crown: commonly $2,500–$6,000+ total, depending on need for bone grafts, sinus lifts, advanced imaging, and provider fees. Prices vary widely.

Where to search for reputable providers in Phoenix
- AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) surgeon locator  
- AAP (American Academy of Periodontology) find-a-periodontist  
- AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) directory  
- ADA Find-a-Dentist and local dental society referrals  
- Read patient reviews and verify credentials/licenses on state board sites

If you want, I can:
- Find highly rated implant specialists in Phoenix near your ZIP code, or  
- Compare 3–5 clinics based on credentials, reviews, and services, or  
- Prepare a checklist you can bring to consultations.

Tell me your ZIP code and whether you need a single tooth implant, multiple implants, or full-arch replacement, and I’ll search for options.
